_what: THE PROTECTED CAPABILITY FLOOR (owner ruling 4, 2026-10-27, KDEC-033). What the security gate must expect whatever scanner-registry.yaml says. Kit-owned: CODEOWNERS names one protected owner for it (KDEC-050; GitHub accepts any one owner on a line, so the owner team holds everyone who may approve). A PR that deletes a scanner's registry row, job and report line still fails: statically and against the PR base (scripts/capability_floor.py --check-tree / --base-floor) and in the security gate itself, over the run's evidence (the capability-floor composite). tests/prove_capability_floor.py is the adversarial test of exactly that deletion.
_shrink: The floor only shrinks through a tombstone (owner ruling 8): capability, the historical scanner identities, decision, approved_by, decided_on, reason, uncovered_gap, and either a replacement capability that is itself in the floor or a gap_decision {approved_by, reference, expires}. An expired gap decision is BREACHED and never restores the removed tool. A tombstone is never deleted: the history it names is permanent.
_held: KE-04 (KDEC-050): scripts/capability_floor.py holds the rule above. Against the base (--base-ref, on pull requests AND pushes) every base tombstone and selection tombstone must be present unchanged, a removal is covered only by a tombstone NEW in that change, every registry scanner row must belong to a floor capability, and a capability_selection candidate removed needs a selection tombstone {selection, candidate, decision, approved_by, decided_on, reason}. A tombstone's authority is the code-owner approval of the change that added it; every gate run lists every tombstone.
_policy: KE-03 seam (KDEC-050, PROPOSED for the owner): the two open questions are one line each below. Defaults are the STRICTER answers: a replacement must cite replacement_proof (a tests/ file naming both capabilities), and a gap decision expires at most 90 days after decided_on (null or 0 = no cap). Loosening either needs a new tombstone_policy.decision.
